candidates.current_role: Tarrant County Judge since 2023
candidates.background: O'Hare has been Tarrant County Judge since January 2023. He earned a BBA in finance from the University of Texas at Austin and a law degree from SMU, and ran a law firm and real estate investment company for more than 25 years. He served on the Farmers Branch City Council and as mayor from 2008 to 2011, and was chairman of the Tarrant County Republican Party. He lives in Southlake.

priorities.text: Campaigns on lower taxes and less spending, citing what he calls the largest property tax cuts in county history.
Says he wants to make Tarrant County the safest large county in Texas and has increased funding for law enforcement.
Highlights election changes he championed, including numbered paper ballots and ending internet-based transmission of results.
Says he wants to keep property taxes down and attract more corporate relocations.

record.text: Under O'Hare the county adopted the maximum 20% homestead exemption for the first time; he says it saves homeowners $262 million.

In September 2025 the court adopted a county tax rate of 18.62 cents per $100 valuation, below the no-new-revenue rate, after an earlier vote was blocked when two Democratic commissioners were absent.
Says the county operating budget fell by $81 million over three years while funding for the sheriff and district attorney rose.
Pushed the 2025 mid-decade redistricting of commissioner precincts, adopted 3 to 2.
In December 2024 the court passed a resolution asking the Legislature to fund a mental health hospital for Tarrant County.
